definitions.explanation: A cooking method and dish in which fish (especially eel) is split, skewered, and grilled while being basted with a sweet soy-based sauce. Most famously applied to eel (unagi), though also used for other fish.

examples.japanese: {鰻|うなぎ}の{蒲焼|かばや}きを{食|た}べた。
{蒲焼|かばや}きのたれは{醤油|しょうゆ}とみりんで{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Kabayaki sauce is made from soy sauce and mirin.

examples.japanese: {土用|どよう}の{丑|うし}の{日|ひ}に{鰻|うなぎ}の{蒲焼|かばや}きを{食|た}べる{習慣|しゅうかん}がある。
examples.english: There is a custom of eating kabayaki eel on the Midsummer Day of the Ox.

notes:
The defining feature is the tare ({蒲焼|かばや}きのたれ) — a sweet, salty sauce of soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar that caramelizes on the fish during grilling.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鰻|うなぎ}の{蒲焼|かばや}き: eel kabayaki (the most iconic form)
- {蒲焼|かばや}きのたれ: kabayaki glaze/sauce
- {鰻丼|うなどん}: eel rice bowl topped with kabayaki eel
- {鰻重|うなじゅう}: kabayaki eel served over rice in a lacquered box

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {塩焼|しおや}き: salt-grilled fish — simpler preparation with no sweet sauce
- {照|て}り{焼|や}き: teriyaki — similar glaze technique, applied to various meats and fish
